exposure: maternal BMI categories (underweight, normal weight, overweight, obesity)
cohort: The study included 160 primigravida women with singleton pregnancies.
finding: Higher maternal BMI categories were significantly associated with increased incidence of hypertensive disorders, gestational diabetes, cesarean deliveries, prolonged labor duration, severe perineal tears, macrosomia, and NICU admissions, while mothers with low BMI were prone to preterm and low birthweight babies.
mod_finding: Higher BMI categories were significantly associated with an increased incidence of cesarean deliveries.
